# Getting started {#sec-getting-started}

You need only one of the two languages to follow this primer. The examples are self-contained scripts that you can run as they are, and then modify.

## Getting the code

Download the repository as a zip file from <https://github.com/RamanLab/sysbio-primer>, or clone it with Git:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/RamanLab/sysbio-primer.git
cd sysbio-primer
```

## Python

Python 3.10 or newer is needed. From the repository folder, create a virtual environment and install the packages the examples use (NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, NetworkX and COBRApy), plus a tiny helper package, `sbp`, that the examples use to save their results and figures:

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate        # on Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install -e .
```

Then run any example, for instance:

```bash
python examples/constraint-based/toy_fba/toy_fba.py
```

## MATLAB

The examples use core MATLAB (R2021a or newer) and, where noted at the top of a script, standard MathWorks toolboxes such as the Optimization Toolbox. Some constraint-based examples need the [COBRA Toolbox](https://opencobra.github.io/cobratoolbox/); each chapter says so where this applies.

Start MATLAB in the repository folder and run, once per session:

```matlab
setup_primer      % adds the small +sbp helper package to the path
```

Then run any example, for instance `run examples/constraint-based/toy_fba/toy_fba.m`.

## What the examples write

Each script prints its main results and writes two kinds of output next to itself, under `out/matlab/` or `out/python/`:

* figures (`fig-*.png`), which are the figures shown in this primer;
* `results.json`, with the key numbers. These files are what the automated checks compare between the two languages.
